requirements.heading: Syntax of encoded-words
requirements.text: The notation of RFC 822 is used, with the exception that white space characters MUST NOT appear between components of an 'encoded-word'.

requirements.heading: Character sets
requirements.text: If unencoded text in an 'encoded-word' contains a sequence which causes the charset interpreter to switch out of ASCII mode, it MUST contain additional control codes such that ASCII mode is again selected at the end of the 'encoded-word'.

requirements.heading: Encodings
requirements.text: Nevertheless, a mail reader which claims to recognize 'encoded-word's MUST be able to accept either encoding for any character set which it supports.

requirements.heading: The "Q" encoding
requirements.text: (3) 8-bit values which correspond to printable ASCII characters other than "=", "?", and "_" (underscore), MAY be represented as those characters.

requirements.heading: The "Q" encoding
requirements.text: (But see section 5 for restrictions.) In particular, SPACE and TAB MUST NOT be represented as themselves within encoded words.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: However, an 'encoded-word' that appears in a header field defined as '*text' MUST be separated from any adjacent 'encoded-word' or 'text' by 'linear-white-space'.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: A "Q"-encoded 'encoded-word' which appears in a 'comment' MUST NOT contain the characters "(", ")" or " 'encoded-word' that appears in a 'comment' MUST be separated from any adjacent 'encoded-word' or 'ctext' by 'linear-white-space'.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: An 'encoded-word' that appears within a 'phrase' MUST be separated from any adjacent 'word', 'text' or 'special' by 'linear-white-space'.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: + An 'encoded-word' MUST NOT appear in any portion of an 'addr-spec'.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: + An 'encoded-word' MUST NOT appear within a 'quoted-string'.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: + An 'encoded-word' MUST NOT be used in a Received header field.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: + An 'encoded-word' MUST NOT be used in parameter of a MIME Content-Type or Content-Disposition field, or in any structured field body except within a 'comment' or 'phrase'.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: The 'encoded-text' in an 'encoded-word' must be self-contained; 'encoded-text' MUST NOT be continued from one 'encoded-word' to another.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: Each 'encoded-word' MUST encode an integral number of octets.

requirements.heading: Use of encoded-words in message headers
requirements.text: Each 'encoded-word' MUST represent an integral number of characters.

requirements.heading: Mail reader handling of incorrectly formed 'encoded-word's
requirements.text: However, a mail reader MUST NOT prevent the display or handling of a message because an 'encoded-word' is incorrectly formed.

requirements.heading: Conformance
requirements.text: A mail composing program claiming compliance with this specification MUST ensure that any string of non-white-space printable ASCII characters within a '*text' or '*ctext' that begins with "=?" and ends with "?=" be a valid 'encoded-word'.

requirements.heading: Examples
requirements.text: Within a 'comment', white space MUST appear between an 'encoded-word' and surrounding text.

requirements.heading: Examples
requirements.text: In order to cause a SPACE to be displayed within a portion of encoded text, the SPACE MUST be encoded as part of the 'encoded-word'.

requirements.heading: Examples
requirements.text: In order to cause a SPACE to be displayed between two strings of encoded text, the SPACE MAY be encoded as part of one of the 'encoded-word's.
